paper_sources.P01: Multi-UAV Adaptive Path Planning Using Deep Reinforcement Learning, IROS 2023

task.value: Cooperative adaptive mapping of an initially unknown binary target variable on a flat 2D terrain using multiple UAVs that choose 3D measurement positions.

observation.actor: Agent ID, remaining budget, egocentric position/boundary map with communicated agent positions and altitudes, local belief, weighted local entropy, current-measurement entropy, and communicated footprint coverage.
observation.critic_extra: Global positions, global belief and weighted entropy, global footprint coverage, and other-agent actions.

action.value: Six discrete fixed-step moves: up, north, east, south, west, down, with invalid and conflicting actions masked.

reward.value: One global team reward based on normalized weighted map-entropy reduction, with affine scaling for training stability.

information_boundary.value: Centralized training uses global state in the critic; decentralized execution uses each UAV's locally available fused belief and communicated measurements in the shared actor.

communication.value: UAVs exchange identifier, position, and current measurement when Euclidean distance is within communication radius D; received measurements update local beliefs.

algorithm.value: COMA actor-critic with a centralized Q critic, decentralized shared actor, on-policy TD(lambda), and a per-agent counterfactual baseline that marginalizes that agent's action while fixing other actions.

evaluation.reporting: mean and standard deviation in ground-truth regions of interest

primary_quantitative_target.setting: 4 agents, 25 m limited communication, synthetic terrains, 50 trials, end of 15-measurement mission

qualitative_target.value: Four-agent synthetic-terrain trajectories and final belief/ground-truth map under the 25 m communication setting.
qualitative_target.reason: The repository does not include the real-world thermal dataset used for the paper's field example; a synthetic trajectory is the closest complete, locally executable original-domain target.

unknowns: Total original training interactions or wall-clock budget.
Formal train/validation split and model-selection seed policy.
Exact alpha and beta values in the paper reward equation; code values are treated separately.
Exact pretrained checkpoint used for published tables.
Public location of the real-world thermal raster used in the qualitative field experiment.

success_definition.s1_r0: Imports, environment reset/step, one bounded COMA update, checkpoint write/load, and one evaluation episode all execute with finite outputs without changing algorithm meaning.
success_definition.full_s1: A later authorized formal run evaluates the frozen quantitative target over 50 missions and produces an auditable synthetic qualitative trajectory/map, with paper-code gaps explained.
